articles.title: Reforma tributária: alíquota de 11,3% da CBS pode valer só em 2027 e mudar depois; entenda | G1
articles.standfirst: Percentual proposto pelo TCU ainda depende de aprovação do Senado. Segundo a Receita Federal, a alíquota será recalculada com base na arrecadação do novo imposto, podendo subir ou cair para manter a carga tributária.
articles.summary: Percentual proposto pelo TCU ainda depende de aprovação do Senado. Segundo a Receita Federal, a alíquota será recalculada com base na arrecadação do novo imposto.
articles.body:
Secretário especial da Receita Federal do Brasil, Robinson Sakiyama Barreirinhas — Foto: Saulo Cruz/Agência Senado

O secretário da Receita Federal , Robinson Barreirinhas, lembrou nesta quarta-feira (18) que, pelas regras da reforma tributária sobre o consumo, a alíquota proposta de 11,3% para o novo imposto federal, se confirmada, valerá apenas em 2027 .

Essa alíquota de referência foi proposta pelo Tribunal de Contas da União (TCU) para a Contribuição sobre Bens e Serviços (CBS), tributo federal criado pela reforma tributária.

A proposta foi encaminhada ao Congresso Nacional, mas ainda precisa ser aprovada. Caberá ao Senado definir, até 15 de dezembro, a alíquota final que será cobrada em 2027.

▶️ Para calcular a alíquota da CBS, técnicos do TCU estimaram quanto seria arrecadado com os tributos que serão substituídos pelo novo imposto. Isso porque uma das premissas da reforma tributária sobre o consumo é manter o atual nível da carga tributária.

Barreirinhas explicou, durante uma transmissão ao vivo do jornal "Valor Econômico", que o Senado pode alterar a alíquota proposta pelo TCU para 2027. Ele ressaltou, porém, que a reforma tributária estabeleceu uma divisão de responsabilidades e uma fórmula matemática para definir o percentual.

▶️ Segundo o secretário, a alíquota de 11,3%, se confirmada pelo Senado, valerá apenas em 2027. O percentual será recalculado para 2028, com base nos dados de arrecadação do primeiro ano de funcionamento do novo imposto.

"Essa alíquota de referência vale só para o ano que vem. Ano que vem a gente tem que refazer o cálculo, agora com mais informações. A gente, quando eu digo, o TCU. A Receita vai mandar nova metodologia de cálculo agora com novos insumos relacionados a esse novo período, e o TCU vai ter condições de fazer um ajuste fino na alíquota, com dados reais da arrecadação da CBS, inclusive em relação à redução da evasão fiscal", disse o secretário.

Segundo Barreirinhas, se a arrecadação com a alíquota de 11,3% superar o previsto , o percentual poderá ser reduzido .

Se a arrecadação ficar abaixo do esperado , por outro lado, a alíquota poderá ser elevada para manter o nível da carga tributária.

"Mas é por isso que o legislador previu a revisão das alíquotas ano a ano, para chegar ao fim do período, em 2032, com a alíquota mantendo a carga tributária de maneira mais certeira", explicou o secretário da Receita Federal.

Um dos principais fatores considerados na revisão da alíquota será o quanto o novo imposto conseguiu reduzir a evasão e a sonegação fiscal .

Outro fator será a arrecadação do Imposto Seletivo , conhecido como "imposto do pecado".

Se o Congresso reduzir as alíquotas propostas pelo governo para o Imposto Seletivo e a arrecadação ficar abaixo do previsto, a alíquota da CBS poderá ter de subir para compensar a diferença.

"Congresso é soberano, mas [o seletivo] tem que manter a carga do IPI. Acho difícil se reduzir, principalmente em relação a cigarro, bebida alcoólica. A tendência é manter ou ampliar. Raciocínio é manutenção da carga global. Havendo redução da arrecadação prevista do seletivo, tem de ter aumento da CBS", explicou Barreirinhas.

articles.title: Um ano depois, fraude do Banco Master deixou prejuízo de R$ 76 bilhões | G1
articles.standfirst: Primeira prisão de Daniel Vorcaro e liquidação do Master em novembro de 2025 expuseram vasto esquema de fraudes e tentáculos do banqueiro nos Três Poderes.
articles.summary: Primeira prisão de Daniel Vorcaro e liquidação do Master em novembro de 2025 expuseram vasto esquema de fraudes e tentáculos do banqueiro nos Três Poderes.
articles.body:
Fachada do Banco Master no Itaim Bibi, na Zona Sul de São Paulo, no dia 19 de novembro de 2025 — Foto: Rovena Rosa/Agência Brasil

Na tarde de 18 de novembro de 2025, o Banco Central anunciou a decretação da liquidação extrajudicial do Banco Master e de várias instituições ligadas ao banqueiro Daniel Vorcaro — que havia sido preso na noite anterior no aeroporto de Guarulhos ao tentar embarcar para o Oriente Médio.

Era o fim da trajetória de quase oito anos de Vorcaro como banqueiro e de uma instituição que havia atraído centenas de milhares de clientes por meio do oferecimento Certificados de Depósito Bancário (CDBs) com remunerações bem acima das praticadas por grandes bancos .

Quando teve sua operação encerrada, o Banco Master, uma instituição que no papel contava com mais R$ 90 bilhões em ativos , tinha apenas R$ 4 milhões em caixa.

Mas a liquidação do Master e a primeira prisão de Vorcaro marcariam apenas o começo da revelação da escala das fraudes executadas pela instituição bancária, que ainda teria forte impacto no mundo político e no Judiciário, expondo a cooptação de autoridades por Vorcaro.

Um ano depois, a quebra do Master deixou um rastro de prejuízos que soma R$ 76 bilhões.

Não foi apenas o Master que teve liquidação determinada pelo BC. De 21 liquidações extrajudiciais decretadas pelo órgão em 2026, 11 envolveram instituições ligadas a Vorcaro ou a pessoas do seu círculo , como o Will Bank, a antiga Reag e o Banco Pleno. A liquidação extrajudicial é uma medida previstas pelo BC quando uma instituição financeira é considerada irrecuperável ou quando há constatação de violações contra o sistema financeiro.

O colapso do Master e de instituições satélites de Vorcaro também resultou na maior operação da história do Fundo Garantidor de Créditos (FGC), mecanismo mantido por contribuições de instituições associadas.

O crescimento exponencial do Master havia sido alavancado pela emissão de CDBs, que são cobertos pelo FGC, que garante ressarcimento de até R$ 250 mil por CPF ou CNPJ, por conglomerado financeiro. O esquema do Master justamente fazia um uso sistemático do FGC como chamariz para convencer clientes a investir em títulos do banco, induzindo-os a acreditar que eram de baixo risco.

E a maior parte da fatura da liquidação do Master acabou ficando justamente com o FGC. O fundo já teve que desembolsar R$ 54,8 bilhões para cobrir o prejuízo do esquema fraudulento liderado por Vorcaro.

Deste valor, cerca de R$ 50 bilhões foram direcionados após a quebra do banco e de empresas associadas a Vorcaro, como o Banco Master de Investimento e o Will Bank. Outros R$ 4,3 bilhões já haviam sido usados no primeiro semestre de 2025, quando o Master ainda operava.

Só no caso do Banco Master, os desembolsos chegaram a R$ 28,8 bilhões, distribuídos para cerca de 570,5 mil credores. No total, o FGC já direcionou pagamentos para mais de 1 milhão de credores de empresas do Grupo Master.

Como o fundo é mantido em sua maioria com recursos de grandes bancos, na prática a conta foi em grande parte bancada por instituições mais longevas como o Bradesco, Banco do Brasil, entre outros. Posteriormente, investigações levantaram a suspeita que a tentativa de compra do Master pela cúpula do Banco de Brasília (BRB) foi movida pelo pagamento de dezenas de milhões de reais em propinas por parte de Vorcaro.

O esquema também provocou prejuízos para o BRB, instituição estatal do Distrito Federal que agora busca provisionar R$ 8,8 bilhões para cobrir perdas com carteiras fraudulentas do Master. A proximidade do BRB com o Master foi justamente um dos primeiros sinais de que havia algo errado com o banco de Vorcaro. O próprio BRB tentou adquirir o Master no primeiro semestre de 2025 , numa operação que foi barrada pelo BC.

Regimes de previdência de servidores estaduais e municipais que compraram CDBs e papéis do grupo Master, e que não contavam com garantia do FGC, perderam mais de R$ 4 bilhões. Só o Rioprevidência, fundo de previdência dos servidores do governo do Rio de Janeiro, tinha quase R$ 1 bilhão em aplicações no Master.

O mesmo ocorreu com empresas com títulos do Master, como a Companhia Estadual de Águas e Esgotos do Rio de Janeiro (Cedae), que somaram perdas de cerca de R$ 2,2 bilhões.

Tentáculos no mundo político e no Judiciário

A quebra do Master e a prisão do Vorcaro também expuseram que o banqueiro desenvolveu uma ampla e suspeita rede de relações com membros dos três Poderes, incluindo dirigentes de órgão públicos, integrantes do Congresso Nacional , políticos de diferentes matizes políticas e até ministros do Supremo Tribunal Federal ( STF ) . A rede ainda se estendia a fundos de pensão de estados e municípios.

Investigações levantaram suspeitas sobre pagamentos, viagens, encontros, contratos com pessoas próximas a autoridades, possíveis informações privilegiadas e articulações políticas em defesa dos interesses do Banco Master.

No Congresso Nacional , aparecem nomes como Ciro Nogueira (PP-PI), senador e ex-ministro da Casa Civil, que mantinha relação próxima com Vorcaro; Hugo Motta (Republicanos-PB), presidente da Câmara, mencionado em conversas e articulações envolvendo o banqueiro; Davi Alcolumbre (União Brasil-AP), presidente do Senado , citado no contexto das relações políticas; e Fábio Faria (PP-RN), ex-ministro das Comunicações.

O senador Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), que está nos EUA, também passou a ser investigado no contexto do Master, após a revelação de que o político de extrema direita negociou repasses de dezenas de milhões de reais diretamente com Vorcaro.

No STF , Alexandre de Moraes aparece em registros de contatos com Vorcaro, enquanto sua esposa, Viviane Barci de Moraes, manteve contrato de R$ 131 milhões com o Banco Master. Dias Toffoli teve seu nome associado a negócios envolvendo o resort Tayayá e fundos relacionados ao universo empresarial do banqueiro.

Também surgiram questionamentos envolvendo Kassio Nunes Marques, após notícias sobre pagamentos ao advogado Kevin Marques, seu filho; e Luiz Fux, cujo filho, Rodrigo Fux, manteve conversas e contatos próximos com Vorcaro. André Mendonça também recebeu o banqueiro em reunião articulada por intermediários.

No Banco Central, órgão responsável pela fiscalização do sistema financeiro, as suspeitas atingiram Paulo Sérgio Neves de Souza, ex-diretor de Fiscalização, e Belline Santana, ex-chefe do Departamento de Supervisão Bancária, ambos afastados em meio a investigações sobre possíveis pagamentos e favorecimento ao Master.

Vorcaro segue preso atualmente no 19º Batalhão da Polícia Militar no Distrito Federal, a Papudinha.

articles.title: Correios: TCU mantém estatal em lista de risco por déficit bilionário | G1
articles.standfirst: Balanço da empresa aponta prejuízo de R$ 7,5 bilhões até o terceiro trimestre de 2026, levando a estatal ao 16º trimestre consecutivo com déficit nas contas.
articles.summary: A estatal acumula perdas líquidas que chegaram a R$ 8,46 bilhões em 2025, gerando alerta do TCU sobre a sustentabilidade dos serviços postais e riscos à União.
articles.body:
O Tribunal de Contas da União (TCU) manteve os Correios na lista de alto risco da administração pública federal diante do "severo agravamento" da situação econômico-financeira da estatal, que acumula prejuízos líquidos nos últimos anos. A lista é divulgada a cada dois anos.

"A materialidade e a urgência do tema decorrem da rápida deterioração financeira da estatal. O resultado líquido passou de um prejuízo de R$ 0,60 bilhão em 2023 para R$ 2,45 bilhões em 2024 e atingiu expressivos R$ 8,46 bilhões em 2025", afirma trecho do documento.

"No primeiro trimestre de 2026, novo prejuízo de R$ 3,16 bilhões evidenciou a aceleração da crise, puxada pela queda na receita líquida anual (de R$ 18,91 bilhões em 2024 para R$ 16,65 bilhões em 2025), diante de custos que se mantiveram rígidos em patamar superior a R$ 15,9 bilhões", complementa o TCU.

O balanço contábil da empresa, divulgado na última semana, aponta prejuízo de R$ 7,5 bilhões até o terceiro trimestre de 2026, levando a estatal ao 16º trimestre consecutivo com déficit nas contas.

O TCU também aponta perda de receitas e de participação de mercado, falhas na execução do plano de reestruturação e fragilidades regulatórias.

Entre os problemas identificados está a ausência de uma metodologia confiável para calcular e financiar os custos da prestação do serviço postal universal em municípios deficitários.

"A sustentabilidade econômico-financeira dos Correios é indispensável para garantir a continuidade dos serviços postais universais em todo o território nacional e prevenir a dependência da empresa em relação a recursos orçamentários do Tesouro. A ECT exerce papel central de integração, atendendo a todos os mais de 5.500 municípios do país, inclusive em localidades remotas e desprovidas de viabilidade econômica", diz o documento.

Ainda em 2025, a empresa apresentou uma série de medidas para reorganizar a companhia, reduzir custos e modernizar seu modelo de negócios.

Entre elas está a contratação de um empréstimo de R$ 12 bilhões com cinco dos principais bancos do país para reforçar o caixa da estatal em meio à crise financeira. A operação conta com garantia do Tesouro Nacional em caso de calote.

Sobre o empréstimo, o TCU avalia que a operação se insere "dentro da necessidade financeira da empresa, estimada em até R$ 20 bilhões".

Ao mesmo tempo, pondera que, "embora atenue pressões de curto prazo, a operação amplia a exposição fiscal do governo federal e não afasta os riscos estruturais associados à sustentabilidade do negócio e à ausência de fontes estáveis para financiar as obrigações da universalização postal".

O tribunal cita ainda fiscalização que acompanhou a execução do Plano de Reestruturação 2025-2027. Em acórdão recente, o TCU identificou inconsistências na demonstração das premissas econômico-financeiras e operacionais, além de fragilidades nos mecanismos de controle.

Segundo a Corte, diversas ações não vinham atingindo as metas estipuladas e, até março de 2026, não havia ocorrido revisão formal das projeções nem definição de medidas compensatórias. O tribunal também apontou indefinições sobre as fontes de financiamento necessárias para a execução integral do plano.

Prejuízo dos Correios triplicou em 2025 e foi de R$ 8,5 bilhões — Foto: Jornal Nacional/ Reprodução

Na avaliação do TCU, os Correios precisam recuperar de forma sustentável sua capacidade econômico-financeira, com medidas efetivas para recompor receitas, reduzir estruturalmente os custos, aumentar a eficiência operacional e modernizar a empresa.

O objetivo é diminuir a dependência de empréstimos extraordinários e de recursos do Tesouro Nacional.

O tribunal também defende que o plano de reestruturação seja executado com premissas financeiras e operacionais fundamentadas e metas realistas.

Para isso, recomenda mecanismos de monitoramento capazes de identificar desvios e permitir a revisão periódica das projeções e a adoção de medidas corretivas.

Outro ponto considerado indispensável é a criação de um modelo sustentável de financiamento, compatível com a capacidade de pagamento dos Correios, que aperfeiçoe a gestão dos riscos fiscais da União e reduza a exposição direta do governo federal.

No âmbito da política postal, o TCU aponta que cabe ao Ministério das Comunicações modernizar o modelo de universalização, aprimorar a supervisão dos custos regulatórios e instituir fontes estáveis de financiamento para as obrigações de interesse público assumidas pela estatal.

articles.title: Banco do Brasil alerta clientes sobre vazamento de dados pessoais | G1
articles.standfirst: Instituição identificou uso indevido de uma credencial válida para acessar informações cadastrais. Banco afirma que senhas e códigos de segurança não foram comprometidos e orienta clientes a redobrar a atenção com possíveis golpes.
articles.summary: Comunicado enviado aos correntistas informa que foram acessados nomes, CPFs, e-mails e dados bancários.
articles.body:
O Banco do Brasil (BB) soma R$ 1,64 bilhão em valores relacionados à renegociação de dívidas rurais em Mato Grosso — Foto: Reprodução

O Banco do Brasil informou nesta quarta-feira (18) que identificou, em 12 de novembro, um acesso não autorizado a dados pessoais de seus clientes.

Segundo comunicado enviado aos correntistas, os dados expostos podem incluir nome, CPF, endereço de e-mail, número da agência e, em alguns casos, número da conta.

O banco afirmou que não houve invasão de seus sistemas nem exposição de senhas ou códigos de segurança. Também não foram identificadas transações financeiras decorrentes do incidente.

De acordo com a mensagem, as apurações indicaram que terceiros utilizaram indevidamente uma credencial válida para acessar os dados. O banco informou que já revogou a credencial, interrompendo o acesso não autorizado, e acionou seus protocolos de segurança assim que identificou o problema.

A instituição também afirmou que está reforçando o monitoramento e adotando medidas de segurança, privacidade e proteção de dados, incluindo as notificações exigidas pela Lei Geral de Proteção de Dados (LGPD).

O principal risco apontado pelo BB é o uso dos dados expostos em tentativas de golpes. Com informações pessoais e de contato dos clientes, criminosos podem enviar mensagens falsas ou se passar pelo banco para tentar obter senhas, códigos de segurança e outras informações.

🔎 Essa prática é conhecida como phishing e consiste em enganar as vítimas para roubar dados pessoais ou financeiros.

O banco orientou os clientes a redobrar a atenção com mensagens e contatos suspeitos.

"O BB não solicita senhas, códigos de segurança, instalação de aplicativos ou movimentações financeiras para supostas contas seguras", destacou o comunicado.

A instituição orientou ainda que mensagens e links suspeitos, além de páginas falsas que utilizem o nome do banco, sejam denunciados pelo e-mail abuse@bb.com.br. Segundo o BB, isso permite adotar medidas junto aos serviços de hospedagem e provedores de acesso e conteúdo na internet.

Em caso de dúvidas, os clientes podem entrar em contato pelos canais oficiais do banco: o Fale Com, disponível no aplicativo do Banco do Brasil; o WhatsApp, pelo número 4001-0001; ou a Central de Relacionamento, pelos telefones 4004-0001 e 0800 729 0001.

articles.title: Gold drops from Rs 1.8 lakh high to Rs 1.31 lakh per 10 grams, yet ETF inflows beat 2025's total as investors buy the dip and build exposure through SIPs and lump-sum buys
articles.summary: Gold prices have been crashing but investors’ appetite for gold ETFs or Exchange Traded Funds remains strong.
articles.body: Gold prices have been crashing but investors’ appetite for gold ETFs or Exchange Traded Funds remains strong. Gold prices have fallen by more than 25% since climbing to a record Rs 1.8 lakh per 10 gm in January, giving investors an opportunity to increase their exposure to the precious metal at lower prices.The demand for gold exchange-traded funds has remained robust. The category attracted around Rs 49,399 crore between January and October 2026, exceeding the Rs 42,961 crore it collected during the whole of calendar year 2025.Why gold ETFs are in demandWealth managers say investors are taking advantage of the correction to add gold to their portfolios, either by making lump-sum purchases or investing gradually through weekly or monthly systematic investment plans (SIPs). The staggered approach also helps them average their purchase costs amid continued price volatility.In October, gold ETFs recorded net inflows of approximately Rs 3,474 crore. Although this was lower than the record Rs 4,451 crore received in September, inflows remained significantly above historical averages, extending the run of strong investor demand for gold-backed funds, according to an ET report.On Wednesday, MCX Gold is trading at around Rs 1.31 lakh per 10 grams.The latest decline has been driven by factors such as a stronger US dollar, rising bond yields and uncertainty surrounding the US interest-rate outlook. However, experts believe investors with a long-term investment horizon can use the price dip to build their gold holdings in stages instead of trying to identify the market bottom.“Gold prices have remained under pressure due to less supportive macro factors, including higher yields, a stronger dollar and rate hikes by central banks,” said Tapan Patel, fund manager, commodities, Tata Asset Management. “The current correction provides an opportunity for investors to rebalance their portfolios and add gold as part of their strategic asset allocation.”Patel believes the long-term investment case for gold remains strong. Purchases by central banks, efforts to diversify away from the US dollar, geopolitical tensions and the possibility of a decline in the dollar's value could continue to provide support to prices.Manav Modi of Motilal Oswal Financial Services told the financial daily that shifting expectations about US monetary policy under the new Federal Reserve chair, Kevin Warsh, have also contributed to the recent correction in gold prices.Gold in free fallGold prices dropped almost 2% on Wednesday, touching their lowest level in more than a year as a stronger US dollar and expectations of higher interest rates weighed on the metal. Investors were also waiting for the minutes of the Federal Reserve’s latest meeting for indications of its future monetary policy.Spot gold was down 1.9% at $3,777.83 an ounce as of 0627 GMT, after slipping to its weakest level since September 2025 earlier in the session. US gold futures for December delivery also declined, losing 2.2% to $3,779.50."The bearish movement in gold prices have been primarily driven by sentiment and technicality, with hawkish reaffirmation from Fed officials and a push up in the US Treasury yields in turn leading to a firmer US dollar," Kelvin Wong, senior market analyst at OANDA was quoted as saying by Reuters.The dollar remained close to a 19-month peak, making gold priced in the US currency costlier for buyers using other currencies.Market participants are now looking to the minutes of the Federal Open Market Committee’s October 27-28 meeting for further clues on the Fed’s policy direction.(Disclaimer: Recommendations and views on the stock market, or any other asset classes or personal finance management tips given by experts and analysts are their own. articles.title: Anthropic IPO: How to buy shares, expected price and risks investors should know
articles.summary: AI giant Anthropic is preparing for its stock market debut, giving individual investors an opportunity to own a stake in the company behind chatbot Claude.
articles.body: AI giant Anthropic is preparing for its stock market debut, giving individual investors an opportunity to own a stake in the company behind chatbot Claude. The initial public offering (IPO) is expected to value the company at $1.4 trillion (£1 trillion), making it one of the biggest stock market listings in history.Investor demand is already strong, with reports suggesting that the offering is nearly six times oversubscribed. However, the IPO comes amid volatility in US markets, particularly technology stocks.Here is what investors need to know about the share price, application process and risks before deciding whether to invest.Anthropic IPO priceAccording to the company's prospectus, Anthropic is offering 825 million shares of Class A common stock at an initial price range of $70 to $78 per share. The final price will be decided on Wednesday.The shares will carry voting rights, but all the votes combined will account for only 49.9% of the total voting power. This means investors will not have enough voting rights to force changes in how the company is run.The shares are scheduled to list on the Nasdaq in New York on Thursday. Both individual investors and large institutions will be able to participate.How can retail investors apply?Investors in the UK can subscribe to Anthropic shares through AJ Bell, Hargreaves Lansdown, Robinhood and eToro. The minimum investment differs across platforms.Robinhood and eToro require a minimum investment of $250 (£189), while Hargreaves Lansdown has set the minimum at £250. AJ Bell requires at least £1,000.The application deadlines are 1pm on Wednesday for AJ Bell and 3pm for Hargreaves Lansdown and Robinhood. All three platforms have warned that applications could close earlier without notice.Those who miss the IPO can still buy shares once they begin trading on the Nasdaq. They will also be available through platforms that are not participating in the offering.Buying Anthropic through mutual fundsDirect investment is not the only way to gain exposure to Anthropic. Some funds already hold stakes in the company.In the UK, these include the Baillie Gifford US Growth and Scottish Mortgage investment trusts. Fidelity also has investments in funds available to US investors.After the listing, Anthropic shares are expected to enter some tracker funds, although the timing will vary. Actively managed funds may also choose to buy the stock. This means investors could gain exposure through their existing fund investments without purchasing shares directly.RisksStrong demand does not necessarily mean the shares will deliver lasting returns. Anthropic's prospectus includes 92 pages detailing potential risks to the company and its industry. Recent volatility in US markets, particularly technology stocks, is another factor investors need to consider.The company's governance structure has also attracted scrutiny. The Guardian's financial editor Nils Pratley has raised concerns, saying it “represents an extraordinary concentration of power in the hands of a few individuals”.Jason Hollands, managing director of investment platform Bestinvest by Evelyn Partners, which is not participating in the IPO, has also highlighted concerns about the company's profitability.“Anthropic would give most retail investors the first opportunity to have a direct stake in a frontier AI developer. But it remains a capital-intensive business, and it has yet to establish a consistent path to profitability,” he told The Guardian. “Investors will need to judge whether the company can turn demand for its models into durable earnings.”Hollands says strong demand and limited share supply could push up the stock initially, but that does not guarantee sustained gains.(Disclaimer: Recommendations and views on the stock market, other asset classes or personal finance management tips given by experts are their own. articles.title: No 24x7 trading in immediate future, Sebi chief flags cyber risks, liquidity concerns
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has no immediate plans to introduce round-the-clock stock market trading, with chairman Tuhin
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) has no immediate plans to introduce round-the-clock stock market trading, with chairman Tuhin Kanta Pandey flagging cybersecurity threats, fragmented liquidity and investor fatigue as key concerns. He said that extending market hours would require a strong justification, given the costs and operational risks involved.Speaking to the media on Wednesday on the sidelines of the 65th General Assembly and Annual Meeting of the World Federation of Exchanges (WFE), Pandey said tha the regulator needs to carefully weigh the potential risks before considering a shift to 24x7 trading."For the 24x7 approach, we should have a very strong kind of reason why should we do it, and what are the costs and what are the risks of that," Pandey told ANI. "Nobody has a clue of how they are going to handle the cybersecurity. Every day something is happening in the US."While he did not comment on extending existing trading hours, Pandey questioned whether longer sessions would necessarily improve market efficiency, pointing to their possible impact on liquidity and retail investors."People will complain that the prices have gone up at night while they were sleeping. Extending the market hours is not necessarily a very efficient way," he said.He also indicated that prediction markets were not a priority for the regulator.Equity tokenisation not feasible for nowOn distributed ledger technology (DLT), Pandey said corporate bond tokenisation was progressing through a three-phase pilot. However, extending the technology to equities was not viable at present because of the scale of India's equity market and the costs involved."Equity is a slightly different cup of tea," he said. "We have to see the efficiency of DLT technologies vis-a-vis equity market cap. DLT cannot handle it, and it will be a very costly technology."Dual listing faces structural hurdlesPandey also highlighted two challenges to allowing Indian companies to list overseas: the absence of full rupee capital account convertibility and India's client-level segregation framework.India tracks individual investors through millions of accounts and around 1,000 clearing members. This differs from markets using omnibus accounts, where clearing corporations have limited visibility into individual end-clients. Aligning the two systems would involve technological challenges, he said."Dual listing would mean that your prices will simply equalize, and all kinds of investors should be capable of trading in all kinds of places," Pandey said.SEBI reviews key market regulationsOn other reforms, Pandey said Sebi was undertaking a comprehensive review of its Issue of Capital and Disclosure Requirements (ICDR), Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements (LODR), and Innovators Growth Platform (IGP) norms, last overhauled in 2018.The regulator is also examining proposals concerning the Margin Trading Facility (MTF) and a pre-IPO platform.On Securities Lending and Borrowing (SLBM), Pandey said India would follow an exchange-traded model instead of opaque over-the-counter practices."We don't want anything dark pool or outside OTC kind of thing. We want it on exchanges," he said, emphasising the need for transparent market frameworks.Money habits form by age 7. Is your child learning the right ones? Join the TOI Money Masterclass.

articles.title: Bombay HC quashes ICICI Bank’s sanction to prosecute ex-CEO Chanda Kochhar
articles.summary: Bombay High Court on Wednesday set aside ICICI Bank’s sanction to prosecute its former CEO Chanda Kochhar in connection with alleged irregularities in
articles.body: Bombay High Court on Wednesday set aside ICICI Bank’s sanction to prosecute its former CEO Chanda Kochhar in connection with alleged irregularities in loans extended to the videocon group, led by Venugopal Dhoot.According to news agency PTI, a single-judge bench of justice Milind Jadhav ruled that the authority granting the sanction had failed to apply its mind to the material placed before it.“The impugned sanction dated May 15, 2023, is illegal and deserves to be quashed on the ground that the authority that granted the same is not a competent authority and it completely failed to apply its mind to the material, or lack thereof, placed before it while granting sanction,” the court observed.The High Court said the sanction order was legally unsustainable and therefore null and void.The court delivered its verdict on a petition filed by Kochhar, who argued that ICICI Bank had not followed the prescribed procedure while approving the sanction for her prosecution.The Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) arrested Kochhar and her husband, Deepak Kochhar, in December 2022 in connection with the alleged loan fraud. The couple received interim bail in January 2023.In June 2023, the CBI told a special court in Mumbai that ICICI Bank had approved the sanction to prosecute Kochhar because there appeared to be a quid pro quo, an exchange of favours in the loan extended to videocon.Such approval is mandatory under the prevention of corruption act because bank employees are treated as public servants under the law.The case relates to a Rs 3,250-crore loan that ICICI Bank sanctioned to the videocon group in 2012, when Kochhar was at the helm of the bank. The CBI has alleged cheating and irregularities in the loan approval process.According to the investigating agency, Kochhar cleared the loan because her husband and family members stood to benefit from the transaction. In return, videocon allegedly invested in Nu renewable, a company linked to her husband, the CBI has claimed.The loan later turned into a non-performing asset (NPA) and was classified as a bank fraud case.Money habits form by age 7. articles.body: NEW DELHI: Cash-strapped budget airline SpiceJet has approved a proposal to raise up to Rs 5,500 crore to strengthen its finances, rebuild its fleet and support its revival.The airline's board cleared the fundraising plan at a meeting on Wednesday, after being briefed on investment discussions with potential new investors. The proposed capital raise will be carried out through a combination of equity and other permitted instruments, subject to the necessary shareholder and regulatory approvals, SpiceJet said in a statement.The board has also approved a proposal to increase the company's authorised share capital from Rs 2,000 crore to Rs 7,500 crore, subject to the required approvals. It has directed the management to expedite the fundraising process.The move comes as SpiceJet faces mounting pressure on its operations and finances. Its domestic market share fell to 0.6% in September from 1.2% in August, according to the latest data from the Directorate General of Civil Aviation (DGCA).The airline attributed the strain to geopolitical disruptions and airspace restrictions, alongside a sharp rise in aviation turbine fuel (ATF) prices, which it said had more than doubled over the past few months. The proposed fundraise is expected to provide funds to strengthen its balance sheet, support fleet expansion and meet operational requirements.Fleet expansion plans amid financial pressureSpiceJet has been working to expand its operational fleet even as it struggles with aircraft groundings, payment pressures and a cash crunch. The airline had announced in September that it had finalised lease agreements with three aircraft operators to induct 20 planes ahead of the winter schedule.The planned additions comprise 15 Boeing and five Airbus aircraft under damp and wet lease arrangements, with phased induction scheduled between mid-October and mid-November.The airline had earlier outlined plans to increase operations to around 200 daily flights during the winter schedule, with higher frequencies on key routes and expanded domestic and international connectivity. It currently operates around nine aircraft from its own fleet, alongside a number of wet-leased planes.SpiceJet had also received Rs 150 crore under the Centre's Emergency Credit Line Guarantee Scheme (ECLGS), the government said in September, adding that the aviation regulator was monitoring the airline's operations and financial position.The carrier is also facing legal and payment-related challenges, including insolvency petitions filed by lessors and claims involving former promoter Kalanithi Maran and KAL Airways.SpiceJet chairman and managing director Ajay Singh said the proposed fundraising would provide an opportunity to rebuild the airline, strengthen operations and restore the brand.Shares of SpiceJet rose nearly 5% to Rs 9.97 apiece in late afternoon trade on the BSE on Wednesday.Money habits form by age 7. articles.summary: There is a growing demand for India’s talent as global artificial intelligence (AI) and technology firms are turning to the country in greater numbers to
articles.body: There is a growing demand for India’s talent as global artificial intelligence (AI) and technology firms are turning to the country in greater numbers to recruit talent and develop products, with startups and mid-sized companies increasingly relying on the country’s engineers for product research and development.Despite India's large pool of engineers, competition for skilled professionals is intense, with domestic and international startups competing against IT services companies, global capability centres (GCCs) and businesses in other sectors, industry experts said.Kapil Joshi, CEO of IT staffing and IT solutions at Quess Corp, said professionals with four to 12 years of experience, capable of implementing AI solutions and taking projects into production, make up 55% of total demand.Growing demand for India’s talentA group of 24 international AI and emerging technology companies, excluding Big Tech, tracked by staffing firm Xpheno, expanded their combined employee strength in India by over 30% in the past year to approximately 24,000.The companies span several segments, including AI, robotics, cybersecurity, fintech and enterprise software. The list includes Anthropic, OpenAI, ElevenLabs, Perplexity, Replit, Wispr Flow, Databricks, Figma, Rippling, Harness and Glean.“India may not be comparable to Silicon Valley today in terms of the depth of its AI talent, but it has the potential,” Kamal Karanth, cofounder of Xpheno told ET.Pointing to the increasing number of emerging technology companies recruiting in India, he said, “From a future investment perspective, companies want to build that capability here.”The US has produced nearly 200 unicorns over the past two years, and many of these companies have access to talent in India, Karanth said.Industry executives, including founders, staffing firms and analysts, attributed the trend to several factors.These include the growing ability of Indian teams to build and customise technology products for global markets, as well as the challenges of recruiting talent in established technology centres such as San Francisco. These factors are prompting international technology companies to establish teams in India and expand their existing operations.Companies such as Rippling and Databricks are primarily interested in India’s engineering workforce, while ElevenLabs and Wispr Flow are expanding locally to serve their growing user base in the country, said Pratyush Choudhury, cofounder and general partner at AI-focused venture fund Activate.“For ElevenLabs and Wispr Flow, India became an important market early on…and they need local teams to adapt and customise their products for Indian users and customers ,” he said. India ranks as the second- or third-largest market outside the US for both companies, he added.Activate invests in early-stage startups working across AI applications, foundational models and infrastructure. Its portfolio includes both ElevenLabs and Wispr Flow.Choudhury, who also works closely with startups on recruitment, pointed to Wispr Flow’s Android product to illustrate how the Indian market has shaped product requirements. The need to address keyboard functionality and mobile usage became apparent as the company catered to Indian users.ElevenLabs, meanwhile, collaborated with Indian startups on developing models and sourcing data to train them.Manav Garg, former executive chairman of Emergent Labs, said the growing presence of founders and senior executives of Indian origin in Silicon Valley is also helping international startups establish operations in India. Garg is launching an agentic commerce startup backed by Flipkart and Navi cofounder Sachin Bansal.“The Indian diaspora in Silicon Valley has a better understanding of the local talent market and can leverage its connections to build teams here,” Garg said.Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Scotch on the rocks? India imposes 162.5% duty, tax on bulk UK imports; domestic production likely to be hit
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: India is imposing an effective duty and tax of 162.5 per cent on bulk Scotch whisky imports from Britain, higher than the 150 per cent levied
articles.body: NEW DELHI: India is imposing an effective duty and tax of 162.5 per cent on bulk Scotch whisky imports from Britain, higher than the 150 per cent levied before the India-UK trade agreement came into force, according to a Reuters report. This comes amid a dispute over customs classification.The higher levy has put liquor companies, including Pernod Ricard and Diageo, in a difficult position, with more than 80 containers of bulk Scotch belonging to Pernod, Diageo and Bacardi reportedly stuck at Indian ports.Under the India-UK trade agreement, implemented on July 15, New Delhi agreed to reduce import duty on certain Scotch whisky products from 150 per cent to 75 per cent.The reduction was welcomed by British exporters and liquor companies that import Scotch in bulk and blend it with Indian spirits to manufacture popular whisky brands.However, it was found that the companies were using incorrect customs classifications for bulk Scotch imports, which are used as raw material in blended whisky production.According to the Reuters report, investigators have said that such imports fall under a new customs classification introduced in May for "compound alcoholic preparations", which attracts a 150 per cent customs duty. An additional consumption tax takes the effective levy to 162.5 per cent, according to a government document reviewed by Reuters.The liquor companies maintain that both bulk and bottled Scotch imports should qualify for the reduced 75 per cent duty under the trade agreement.With the investigation under way, authorities have allowed provisional release of the consignments. Under the arrangement, companies must pay duty equivalent to 75 per cent of the goods' value upfront, while the remaining amount is to be secured through bank guarantees, Reuters reported.Pernod Ricard and Diageo have moved to arrange bank guarantees and other funding to secure the release of their consignments, while Bacardi is still considering its options, according to the report.The higher levy has also raised concerns over possible disruptions to domestic whisky production. Mumbai-listed liquor companies Radico Khaitan, Allied Blenders and Distillers, and Tilaknagar Industries, which also import bulk Scotch, are among those under scrutiny.Smaller companies could face greater financial pressure in arranging bank guarantees, particularly if collateral is required. Such guarantees also have to be reported as contingent liabilities.A liquor industry executive told Reuters that companies had little alternative but to arrange the guarantees, as maintaining production was critical, despite the pressure on working capital.Around 80 per cent of Scotch whisky imports from Britain by volume arrive in bulk, according to industry estimates. India is the largest market for Scotch whisky by export volume.Most bulk imports are used to manufacture Indian-Made Foreign Liquor (IMFL) whisky by blending Scotch with other spirits. These products are generally sold at lower prices than fully imported brands such as Chivas Regal and Johnnie Walker.The dispute has also drawn the attention of the British government, which has repeatedly said it is working with New Delhi to resolve the issue and ensure British businesses can export under the tariff terms agreed in the trade pact.India has said the matter will be resolved soon. However, a confidential memo by Indian investigators, reported by Reuters, said any misclassification under the India-UK agreement must stop, citing "substantial revenue implications" for the government.The Scotch Whisky Association has estimated that the trade agreement could increase Scotch exports to India by $1.34 billion over five years.The additional consumption tax has come as a surprise to the liquor industry, with one industry source describing the move to Reuters as a "googly".Money habits form by age 7. articles.title: Anthropic IPO: Why token usage could become a key metric for AI investors
articles.summary: Token usage has become a focal point of AI lab revenue growth. But some industry watchers say they need more of the math behind the metric.
articles.body:
With Anthropic ( ANT ) heading toward the public markets on Thursday , industry watchers say AI token usage could become an increasingly important metric for investors, much like subscriber counts were for video streaming services. But they also warn that token usage remains an opaque measure to assess.

Most of Anthropic's revenue comes from customers paying based on how much they use its AI models, a pricing structure the frontier lab describes in its IPO filing as "metered in tokens and priced according to the model selected." A token is a small chunk of text, roughly a short word or part of a word, that an AI model reads or generates.

In an amended filing this month, Anthropic reported $33.2 billion in revenue for the first nine months of 2026, up from $16.3 billion in the first half of the year. During the first six months, consumption-based revenue, which is tied to customer usage and measured in tokens, accounted for roughly 80% of sales, while subscription-based revenue made up the remaining 20%.

Industry bulls point out that even as token prices have fallen across the industry, lower model rates can make AI cheaper to use, thereby driving higher consumption. AI frontier lab: OpenAI CFO Sarah Friar recently noted higher usage after cutting prices on Luna, its cheapest model series.

"We saw use go up 10x," Friar said last month. "So that tells you there's a lot of price elasticity of demand right now."

Anthropic said in its filing that a growing number of business customers have signed multiyear contracts with minimum-spend commitments that cannot be canceled and with locked-in pricing. Even with those contracts, Anthropic only books revenue as tokens are actually consumed.

But without total token volume or data showing how much Anthropic actually earns per token, industry watchers point out investors cannot tell how much growth comes from discounted enterprise commitments versus steady demand or how much committed spending remains unused.

This is where Claire Husson-Citanna, founder of Bondcoins and formerly FX swap line principal at the Federal Reserve Bank of New York, sees an opportunity: Investors would likely reward labs that disclose not just how much customers have prepaid in token credits, but also how much they actually use and how future revenue and costs are expected to grow.

That visibility matters as cheaper open-weight rivals and advances in quantum computing threaten to put downward pressure on token prices , even as Anthropic faces commitments of nearly $900 billion in long-term computing and infrastructure spending.

articles.title: Anthropic’s registered trademark does not rule out passing-off claim: Lawyer
articles.summary: Belagavi firm says lawsuit vs US-based Anthropic can proceed as a passing-off claim without a registered trademark; court to hear reply Nov 23.
articles.body: Belagavi: Belagavi-based Anthropic Softwares has argued before the Belagavi District Commercial Court that its suit against US-based AI company Anthropic is maintainable even though it does not have a registered trademark.The argument follows the defendant’s contention at the previous hearing that the suit was not maintainable without a registered trademark. The defence had also questioned the jurisdiction of the Belagavi Commercial Court.Appearing for the plaintiff on Tuesday, advocate M M Sheikh argued that the dispute concerns passing off rather than trademark infringement. While an infringement claim generally requires a registered trademark, a passing-off action can be brought even without registration, he submitted.He argued that the plaintiff was entitled to seek legal protection where the cause of action arose. He also contended that registration of a trademark does not give a company the right to exploit another business’s established goodwill or automatically protect it from a passing-off action.He submitted that Anthropic Softwares had built its reputation through years of investment and business development, and alleged that the defendant was attempting to exploit the goodwill of the Belagavi-based company.“The Anthropic Softwares company was registered in 2017 and has remained operational since then. It has invested considerable resources, time and effort to nurture this business like a child. Now, a foreign entity is attempting to destroy it. Such exploitation must be restrained,” he argued.Referring to Section 27(2) of the Trade Marks Act, 1999, Sheikh said it preserves the right to initiate passing-off proceedings irrespective of whether a trademark is registered. He argued that Sections 28 and 29, cited by the defendant, deal with rights arising from trademark registration and infringement of registered trademarks, respectively.Countering the defendant’s contention that Anthropic India Pvt Ltd, Bengaluru, was a separate legal entity from its US-based parent, Sheikh said the Indian company was a subsidiary and that its relationship with the parent should be considered in the dispute.On jurisdiction, he referred to Sections 15 and 21 of the Commercial Courts Act, 2015, arguing that intellectual property disputes, including those involving trademarks and domain names, qualify as commercial disputes under the Act.The defendant’s counsel sought time to file a brief reply to the allegations. articles.summary: Nearly Rs 2 lakh crore in sovereign capital is available for India’s startup ecosystem; govt plans long-term AIFs and RDI loans to boost deeptech.
articles.body: BENGALURU: Nearly Rs 2 lakh crore in sovereign capital is available across central and state govt funding initiatives, a senior govt official said on Wednesday, urging India’s venture capital industry to build larger funds and step up investments in deeptech startups.“If I combine the total fund which is moving from the central government and the state governments, almost Rs 2 lakh crore is available as a sovereign capital to the ecosystem,” said SP Singh, nodal officer in charge of the Centre’s Rs 1 lakh crore Research, Development and Innovation (RDI) Fund, at the Bengaluru Tech Summit 2026 on Wednesday.Singh also disclosed plans for a govt-backed alternative investment fund (AIF) that could remain invested in deeptech companies for 25 years. He said the RDI Fund was designed to offer long-term loans at zero or ultra-low interest rates, reducing the need for startups to dilute ownership at an early stage.Naganand Doraswamy, founder and managing partner of Ideaspring Capital, flagged the mismatch between traditional venture capital investment cycles and the needs of deeptech companies.He said deeptech businesses often needed 12-15 years to mature, while many investors were reluctant to lock up capital beyond four or five years. “That is still the mindset that people have as LPs in India,” he said, referring to investors in venture funds.Arijit Dutt, chief general manager at SIDBI, said the Startup India Fund of Funds 2.0 had a dedicated allocation for deeptech-focused funds, allowing fund lifespans of up to 15 years. articles.title: Nike signals slow stride ahead
articles.summary: Nike has charted its Swoosh-shaped recovery, but it will take time.
articles.body:
Nike last held an investor day nine years ago. Since then, shares are down 36%, including a 79% drop from its October 2021 peak. On Tuesday, Nike returned before investors and outlined its plans to restore the company to greatness.

Full Stride Ahead: Nike launched its " Full Stride Ahead " strategy to get closer to athletes (defined as anyone with a body) and focus on the greatest opportunities for long-term growth. These are the storylines to watch as the company charts its Swoosh-shaped recovery.

Patience required: Nike doesn't expect to return to market-level revenue growth until fiscal 2029, with declines moderating in fiscal 2028. Investors were already restless with the pace of the recovery effort, but they'll need much more patience. Above-market growth may not come until 2030.

Function over form: Nike expects to generate $5 billion in incremental revenue growth from 2028 through 2031. Performance products will drive $4 billion of that growth, leaving behind an era when lifestyle was the lifeblood. Nike Sportswear, Jordan, and Converse account for the other $1 billion, and Jordan won't return to growth until FY2029.

Running for its life: The company wants to replicate its success in running, which has delivered nine consecutive quarters of growth. There's still work to do: The brand is No. 3 in market share in running shoes priced over $110 (it was No. 5 a year ago). Running will drive $1 billion in revenue growth by 2031.

New energy needed: Only 10% of Nike Sportswear revenue comes from new models, demonstrating the brand's over-reliance on icons. By 2031, Nike wants that percentage to hit 40%, which will require innovation. The Air Force 1, Air Jordan 1, Dunk, and Chuck Taylor will account for $6 billion in revenue in FY27, down massively from $13 billion in FY24.

Moving faster: Nike is emphasizing speed, making the product closer to consumers and putting it in their hands while it still matters (remember when it ran out of World Cup inventory?). By 2031, the company will double the volume of products it creates in under 14 months. It will also increase near-shore production volumes in North America by 50%.

Fixing the China problem: China has been a sore spot for Nike, with revenues falling 26% last quarter. The company plans to address it with locally created products, city-specific initiatives, and a streamlined, elevated retail presence. Revenue will continue to fall in China in FY2027 and FY2028, returning to growth in FY2029. See point No. 1 re: patience.

articles.title: APTEL issues notices to HERC, Haryana govt in Eleven Power case
articles.summary: NEW DELHI: The Appellate Tribunal for Electricity (APTEL) on Wednesday directed Haryana Electricity Regulatory Commission (HERC) and Haryana govt to file
articles.body: NEW DELHI: The Appellate Tribunal for Electricity (APTEL) on Wednesday directed Haryana Electricity Regulatory Commission (HERC) and Haryana govt to file their replies within two weeks on an appeal challenging the decision to withhold the implementation of a distribution licence granted to Eleven Power for Gurugram and Nuh.The matter will come up for further hearing on Dec 2.HERC had on Oct 19 allowed a 25-year licence to be granted to Medanta co-founder Sunil Sachdeva–led Eleven Power Private Ltd (EPPL) for setting up a parallel power distribution network in the two Haryana districts under Section 14 of the Electricity Act, 2003, which permits more than one distribution company to operate in the same area. The licence covered Gurugram City, Gurugram Sub-urban, Manesar, Sohna and Nuh, with electricity supply expected to begin in FY2027-28.The Haryana govt, however, invoked Section 108(1) of the Act and asked the power regulator on Oct 26 not to “create, operationalise or effectuate” a parallel distribution licence anywhere in the state. Acting on the directives, HERC issued an order on Oct 28, saying it had decided not to proceed further with the matter, while rejecting EPPL’s request for advance notice and a hearing on any proceedings concerning the licence. Warren's criticism concerns vertical integration, a business structure in which one corporate group owns companies operating at different stages of the same industry. The proposal is part of a broader initiative launched by the American Economic Liberties Project, a nonpartisan coalition bringing together healthcare practitioners, patients, employers, workers and policy advocates seeking structural changes to the healthcare system.

ElevenLabs also works with Razorpay on applications ranging from merchant onboarding to customer retention. Junior writers could now use AI to generate ideas and take on responsibilities previously handled by senior colleagues.The executives, however, stressed that poorly designed automation could frustrate customers. Through Bajaj Finserv Intelligence, we are investing in indigenous research that meets these requirements while applying advanced AI to real-world business challenges,” he said.Rajeev Jain, vice chairman and managing director of Bajaj Finance, said reasoning-led models could make AI deployment more economical for financial services companies while allowing them to retain control over data. He said the models could also help lenders serve customers in Indian languages. “Soket AI’s efficient reasoning-led models can make advanced AI economically viable for financial services, while allowing us to deploy it securely within our own infrastructure, with full control over data,” he said.Abhishek Upperwal, founder and CEO of Soket AI, said the investments would support the company's efforts to develop foundation models and AI systems for critical sectors. articles.title: These bipartisan bills would solve major problems. Why aren’t they already law?
articles.summary: National Taxpayers Union vice president Thomas Aiello urged Congress during its lame-duck session to pass 13 bipartisan bills, including the Warrior Right to Repair Act and the Taxpayer Assistance and Service Act, to reduce waste and improve government efficiency.
articles.body:
In an era defined by razor-thin majorities, partisan gridlock, and seemingly endless political battles, finding common ground across the aisle can feel like an impossible task. Yet, despite the dysfunction that often dominates headlines, Congress has shown that bipartisan cooperation is still possible when lawmakers are willing to put politics aside and focus on delivering results for the American people.

In fact, 13 bipartisan bills offer a promising example of lawmakers working across the aisle to cut through partisan gridlock and advance meaningful policy solutions.

Everyone knows the repair shop at the car dealer rips you off — and customers would be even worse off if drivers could only have their vehicles serviced at the dealer. Yet this is effectively what happens when military equipment is repaired. Many U.S. defense contractors enjoy exclusive rights to repair the military equipment they manufacture. That means even the highly skilled military service members aren’t allowed to fix the mission-critical weapons and equipment they train with every day.

Taxpayers shouldn’t have to pay for exclusive and expensive repairs any more than they should be required to take their car to the dealer every time the check engine light goes on. The Department of Defense should be able to receive technical data necessary to maintain and repair important systems without going back to the manufacturer.

That’s why the Warrior Right to Repair Act , along with 12 other bills, is on National Taxpayers Union’s 2026 No-Brainer report , a list of legislation with real wins for taxpayers that Congress should take up in its lame-duck session. Even after a divisive midterm election season, it’s safe to say everyone agrees the government should work better and cost taxpayers less. Taxpayers should not be forced to pay for fraud, waste and inefficiency.

Americans know the frustration of government inefficiency all too well. Just ask any taxpayer who’s ever called the IRS — you’ll hear about long wait times, disputes that don’t get resolved, major technology limitations and the like. The IRS is long overdue for reform.

It’s now within reach through the Taxpayer Assistance and Service Act, awaiting action in the House of Representatives. If the bill passes, taxpayers will be able to see their communication with the IRS and respond online. They’ll know the status of their refunds. They’ll have the option to have a call back instead of waiting on hold for hours. Their ability to challenge IRS decisions would expand, and they’ll enjoy more rights as taxpayers.

The Senate already approved the bill. The House should take it up immediately before all the progress for taxpayers contained in this bill dies with the new Congress.

Congress should also make better use of the information the federal government already has available.

The federal government is so big, it’s difficult to keep track of programs already in place. That’s why another no-brainer would be passing the Duplication Scoring Act , which would require review of duplicative or overlapping program proposals. Congress should know if a bill under consideration would recreate another program already in operation. Taxpayers don’t need two of everything.

Meanwhile, the federal government should use tools already in place to fight fraud and improper payment, such as the Department of Treasury’s Do Not Pay system. One of the most common causes of improper payments is a failure to verify recipient and eligibility information before payments are made by the government. Expanding the use of the Do Not Pay system is one of the Government Accountability Office’s top recommendations to combat fraud. Congress should pass the Pre-Payment Fraud Prevention and Treasury Data Access Act immediately.

These bills are targeted solutions to real problems that have already been identified. Even though the country seems to be deeply divided, taxpayers, Republicans, Democrats, and independents alike agree the government should work better and safeguard dollars from waste, fraud and abuse. Congress should put these bills and other No-Brainers at the top of its lame-duck agenda.

Thomas Aiello is vice president of federal affairs at National Taxpayers Union.

articles.title: What’s causing all these outages? The internet is held together with shoestring and bubblegum
articles.summary: The fragility of our online systems was on display this past week after back-to-back-to-back outages disrupted flights, global business and national security systems.
articles.body: The fragility of our online systems was on display this past week after back-to-back-to-back outages disrupted flights, global business and national security systems. No one should be shocked: The internet is a loosely connected patchwork project reliant on some seriously outdated systems containing numerous vulnerabilities – many of which we are just discovering. An apt xkcd cartoon visualizes “all modern digital infrastructure” as a giant Jenga-style tower supported by one, thin, vertical block with the label: “a project some random person in Nebraska has been thanklessly maintaining since 2003.” AI has given security researchers a vastly improved capability to find those weak supports and strengthen them. But bad actors have the same tools, and they’re scoping out ways to target weak structures and exploit them. The race is on. AI is sending companies and the government into overdrive to keep adversaries out. But in the process, some companies appear to be pushing out security updates that weren’t ready for primetime. Each of the mega-outages of the past week appears to have a different root cause. Forensics takes time, and the exact cause of each disruption isn’t yet known. Early indications seem to rule out a coordinated attack. But they all appear to share a common vulnerability: The technologies supporting the internet just weren’t built for a world in which online systems are so interconnected and computers can find and exploit weaknesses faster than humans can. “These events do not fill me with confidence about the resilience of our digital infrastructure,” said Matthew Green, member of the Johns Hopkins Information Security Institute. Don’t be shocked if these outages keep happening. The Titanic One of those Jenga blocks is PHP, a programming language most people have probably never heard of – even though it powers 70% of the world’s websites. Researchers using AI agents this summer discovered a method to exploit a PHP vulnerability that could allow an attacker to read passwords, steal entire databases or take over websites. It was patched last month. But the fact that a decades-old tool supporting nearly three-quarters of the websites held a major flaw underscores the problem the internet faces. “We’re dependent on so many things we’ve never even heard of behind the scenes that keep society running,” said Stuart Madnick, an IT security professor at MIT. “In that regard, we’ve become tremendously vulnerable to things we don’t even know about until something goes wrong.” That’s why another decent analogy for the state of today’s internet is the Titanic. The ocean liner’s watertight bulkheads were unable to withstand a failure that exceeded the ship’s architects’ worst-case-scenario assumptions. Even the best-designed systems sometimes succumb to threats and problems that the designers couldn’t have imagined when they built them, noted Rebecca Krauthamer, CEO and cofounder of QuSecure, a cryptography provider for the US government. Now those threats include AI. Agents can work faster and longer than humans, making them particularly useful at finding security holes by employing trial and error techniques. A yet-unproven but widely held theory from security experts about the reason for the recent string of outages is the rush to patch and beat bad actors to the punch. Those expedited updates may contain bugs themselves, causing system outages. “Sometimes you do a patch, you push an upgrade in a system, it behaves abnormally, and it tips over, so to speak,” said Chris Krebs, former United States Director of the Cybersecurity and Infrastructure Security Agency, in an interview with CNN’s Pamela Brown on Tuesday. “I think that’s a lot of what we’ve seen with Microsoft, maybe, and with the FAA last week.” Meanwhile, autonomous AI agents are increasingly overwhelming networks with unprecedented traffic demands, noted Claire Le Goues, computer science professor at Carnegie Mellon University. For example, Microsoft said its systems went down under the weight of a massive traffic load, and they failed to restore themselves because of a bug that was deployed during an update. The FAA’s initial assessment of a massive outage that led to a nationwide ground stop was that a router update sent out bad traffic, which then overwhelmed its networks. It’s not clear that AI was to blame for either outage, but those are the kinds of conditions that are increasingly prevalent across networks. “AI may become the stress test that exposes weaknesses we’ve been living with for decades,” said Krauthamer. What’s next? The good news, perhaps, is these incidents appear thematically related but not part of some coordinated cyberattack by a foreign adversary. As my colleague John Miller notes, we can’t rule that out just yet, but these incidents don’t carry most of the hallmarks of a massive system intrusion. The bad news, however, is that the lack of evidence of a cyberattack shouldn’t give us any comfort: If our systems are this vulnerable without a cyber intrusion, imagine what adversaries could do if they were trying to attack us. “It means that even when our enemies are not trying to attack us, we can attack ourselves just because the systems are so complex and fragile,” said Richard Clarke, former US counterterrorism czar for the George H.W. Bush, Clinton and George W. Bush administrations, in an interview with CNN’s Michael Smerconish on Saturday. So, while the events of the past week may not be surprising, they should be a wake-up call. Some experts advocate for a massive, coordinated effort to harden our digital critical infrastructure. “We are learning again and again that incremental fixes to our infrastructure are no longer sufficient to maintain the resilient systems we need in place,” Krauthamer said. “Our systems must evolve resilience in a way we’ve never faced in the past.” But some are skeptical that will happen. These problems happen in spurts, rise in the public consciousness, then fade when the systems are restored. “We’re not doing a good job learning about these things,” said Madnick, who has been teaching about IT security for five decades. The lack of resource dedication to the underlying problem – ancient systems supporting modern threats – raises the vulnerability of an even more serious problem in the future. “I keep saying the worst is yet to come,” said Madnick. “So far, I haven’t been proven wrong.”

articles.title: Was ‘Grand Theft Auto VI’ worth the 13-year wait? The reviews are in
articles.summary: The review embargo lifted on Wednesday morning, hours before the Thursday release date, and more than 150 critics shared their assessments of Rockstar Games’ long-awaited return to Vice City.
articles.body: “Grand Theft Auto VI” is as grand as every gamer expected it to be. The review embargo lifted on Wednesday morning, hours before the Thursday release date, and more than 150 critics shared their assessments of Rockstar Games’ long-awaited return to Vice City. And the reviews really couldn’t be any better. “Grand Theft Auto VI does something impossible — it lives up to the hype,” The Verge’s Andrew Webster wrote. WIRED’s Boone Ashworth is even more straightforward with this headline: “I will never stop playing Grand Theft Auto.” On Metacritic, the game’s aggregate score is a jaw-dropping 99, which means it ranks as the #1 game of all time. The only other title with a 99 score is 1998’s “The Legend of Zelda: Ocarina of Time.” Rockstar is no stranger to this kind of critical acclaim: Two previous installments in the franchise, 2008’s “GTA IV” and 2013’s “GTA V,” also rank near the top of Metacritic’s all-time list. Some fans wondered whether “VI” could live up to their exceedingly high expectations, given that the new title had been in the works for 13 years and had been delayed multiple times along the way. The critical consensus is that the Rockstar developers met the challenge. Critics have been particularly impressed by the Bonnie-and-Clyde-like romance at the heart of the game, which follows Jason and Lucia as they try to escape a life of crime. “The series matures beyond its memorable car crashes and stickups with a game about love, relationships and nurturing your partner,” Yussef Cole wrote for The New York Times. “Lucia and Jason’s relationship builds on itself and becomes a constant, supportive presence. It gets reflected in the story missions too, as your characters make scripted choices that reflect how you behaved toward each other in the idle moments in between.” Some reviewers sounded mesmerized. “This is a world that feels more lived-in and real than anything I’ve ever played,” IGN’s Luke Reilly wrote, hailing the game as “Unprecedented. Unbelievable. Unmissable.” The Guardian’s Keza MacDonald said, “Rockstar has created the most extraordinarily, indulgently detailed virtual world that we have yet seen. Reviewing it feels a bit like trying to review, say, Paris: it contains so many potential experiences that it’s hard to know where to start.” Ars Technica’s Kyle Orland described being “slack-jawed at the details,” including “a laptop screen partially reflected in a character’s glasses” and “the finger smudges visible on your cell phone in bright sunshine.” Forbes’ Paul Tassi was so struck by the fictional city’s realism that he actually felt guilty about breaking traffic laws. “The first time I ran a red light in Grand Theft Auto 6, I cringed,” he wrote. “It was just too real.” The Washington Post’s Gene Park said it “brings the wonder back” to video gaming. “Writing about this game feels like sending dispatches from the future,” Park wrote. “I’ve been desperate to tell people what happened there, as if I’ve returned from a new life. That is a rare gift from a work of entertainment: to make experience give way to curiosity. Technology built this world, but the writing and understanding of human behavior make it come alive. It raises the bar at every level that matters. ‘Grand Theft Auto VI’ is the most extraordinary game I’ve ever reviewed.” These assessments will certainly make it easier for anyone who’s been on the fence about dropping $80 for the new game. Millions of people have already pre-ordered their copies. “GTA” devotees are putting aside work and household tasks “to set off on a personal side mission to get as much out of the launch as possible,” CNN‘s Teddy Brown wrote. One gamer told Brown he’s taking two weeks off from work and has “a fully scheduled spreadsheet with slots for playing the game, sleeping, and taking breaks for meals and showering.” A married father of two plans to play from midnight to 5 a.m., when he’ll start making breakfast for his family. Some employers are even accommodating the gamers: Logitech is giving its employees the day off for the release. The launch officially began in New Zealand, then Australia, as Rockstar has turned on access time zone by time zone as the clock strikes midnight Thursday. In New Zealand, Twitch streamers showed viewers around the virtual world, though some fans don’t want any bit to be spoiled in advance.

Critics have also praised the game’s deeply immersive nature, which allows players to freely explore Vice City, an intricately detailed fictional version of Miami.

For a lot of retirees, gold was the part of the portfolio that wasn't supposed to move. It was the money set aside for the day stocks fell apart. This year, gold did the falling.

articles.title: Ford is 'officially in the battery business' as its first Fathom cells ship — built on Chinese tech
articles.summary: Ford announced on Wednesday the first lithium iron phosphate battery cells are coming off the line at its BlueOval Battery Park Michigan, part of a plan that...
articles.body:
Ford ( F ) announced on Wednesday that the first lithium iron phosphate (LFP) battery cells are coming off the line at its BlueOval Battery Park Michigan, as part of a plan to license China's CATL battery designs. The move comes against the complicated backdrop of using Chinese tech in US made components.

The batteries are headed to Ford's Louisville Assembly Plant in Kentucky to power prototypes of the Fathom, Ford's upcoming midsize electric pickup. Ford hopes to build an EV cheap enough to win over gas truck buyers, with the Fathom set to start under $30,000 — and key to that is using lower-cost batteries.

"Ford is officially in the battery business. We'll be the first to deliver LFP batteries in the US for mainstream consumer automotive use, and I couldn't be prouder of the Ford team," CEO Jim Farley said on X .

LFP batteries don't use nickel or cobalt, which Ford said helps hold down costs, and the chemistry holds up over years of charging. Ford went with prismatic, or rectangular, cells that fit directly into the chassis. That makes the battery pack part of the truck's structure and cuts costs.

Ford said the Michigan lines can produce 40 cells per minute, making them among the fastest LFP prismatic lines outside China.

But the technology inside those cells produced some controversy.

Ford said its search for a proven LFP design "led us to the world's leading battery manufacturer, CATL," the Chinese giant whose batteries power 30 million vehicles globally. Ford called the deal a "limited technology-licensing and services agreement," not a joint venture. It says it owns the plant, controls operations, and employs the workforce.

That hasn't satisfied Washington. In a letter to Farley sent in early September, Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy expressed "profound concern" over Ford's "reliance on technologies of foreign adversaries." He cited the CATL tech in Marshall, Ford's joint factory with Geely in Spain, and its talks with BYD on hybrid components.

Chief communications officer Mark Truby called it a "head-scratcher of a letter" that came "a week after [the] White House touted the very same job-creating Michigan project he's questioning."

Ford's official response called the letter a "wrongheaded attempt to capture headlines."

With that in the rearview mirror (for now), Ford plans to have its battery pack plant in Marshall running in 2027, ahead of the Fathom's launch. Ford said what it learns there will also feed Ford Energy, its battery energy storage business, which is preparing production in Glendale, Kentucky.

articles.title: Jensen Huang and Howard Lutnick will appear publicly before a powerful Senate panel
articles.summary: The flood of Capitol Hill interest in the ongoing scandal at Nvidia could lead to a traffic jam of high-profile hearings in the weeks ahead.
articles.body:
The flood of Capitol Hill interest in the ongoing scandal at Nvidia ( NVDA ) could create a traffic jam of high-profile hearings in the weeks ahead, including closely watched public grillings by the Senate's powerful banking panel of two of the figures at the center of ongoing national security questions.

A source in Sen. Tim Scott's office confirmed to Yahoo Finance on Wednesday that both ousted Nvidia CEO Jensen Huang and Commerce Secretary Lutnick have agreed to appear publicly before the Senate Committee on Banking, Housing, and Urban Affairs, as talks continue over the precise timing.

Scott said on CNBC earlier on Wednesday that he wants to get the testimony done "before Christmas." He had previously requested in a letter that Huang appear on Dec. 3 and Lutnick appear on Dec. 10.

The Commerce Department previously confirmed Lutnick's willingness to appear before the Senate panel, but the confirmation that the testimony will be public — in front of reporters and cameras — sets up what is expected to be one of Washington's most highly anticipated business-world hearings in years as both men face questions about Huang's affair with an alleged Chinese spy and whether the Trump administration did enough in response to apparent attempts to evade US export controls of advanced semiconductor chips.

The questions will come from Republicans and Democrats, including ranking member Elizabeth Warren, the top Democrat on the committee, who is expected to take the committee's gavel in 2027 when Democrats assume control of the chamber.

Warren has previously accused Huang of "putting our national security at risk" and has promised investigations of her own .

Another Democrat on the panel is Sen. Ruben Gallego of Arizona, who this week posted "slow your roll there" in response to Huang saying he would be honored to return to the company.
